#!/bin/bash
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: --job-name=SM_HSP_dimer_prod
#flux: -t 24:00:00

# The original script requested 20 single-threaded tasks for a multi-threaded application.
# This is a contradiction. The 'gmx mdrun -nt 20' command indicates the user wants to run
# one process with 20 threads. This is translated to 1 task with 20 CPUs.
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 20

# The original script specified separate output and error files.
# Flux merges stderr with stdout by default when a single output file is specified.
# The '%j' variable is replaced with Flux's '{job.id}'.
#flux: -o job.{job.id}.out

# The following Slurm directive for account was not translated as it is not a standard Flux option.
# It must be filled in by the user.
# #SBATCH -A youraccount

# It is always best to do a ml purge before loading modules in a submit file
ml purge
ml ABINIT/8.10.3 Armadillo/9.700.2 CDO/1.9.5 GOTM/5.3-221-gac7ec88d NCO/4.8.1 NCO/4.9.2 OpenFOAM/6 OpenFOAM/7 OpenFOAM/v1912 Rosetta/3.7 Siesta/4.1-MaX-1.0 Siesta/4.1-b4 Singular/4.1.2 XCrySDen/1.5.60 XCrySDen/1.6.2 deal.II/9.1.1-gcc deal.II/9.1.1-intel

ml gromacs/2019.6.th

gmx grompp -f md.mdp -c npt.gro -t npt.cpt -p topol.top -o md_0_1.tpr

# The '-nt 20' argument to gmx mdrun correctly utilizes the 20 CPUs requested by the '-c 20' directive.
# This is a single-process, multi-threaded job, so 'flux run' is not needed.
gmx mdrun -nt 20 -deffnm md_0_1

issues: The script loads an extremely long list of modules, most of which appear to be unused by the `gromacs` application. This can increase job startup time and introduces many unnecessary dependencies, making the environment less reproducible.

#!/bin/bash
#project name
#SBATCH -A youraccount
#specify job name
#SBATCH -J SM_HSP_dimer_prod
#set places for error and output files
#SBATCH --error=job.%j.err
#SBATCH --output=job.%j.out
#request a certain number of hours for the run HR:MIN:SEC
#SBATCH -t 24:00:00
# specify number of cores you want
#SBATCH -n 20
# specify number of threads per task
#SBATCH -c 1

# It is always best to do a ml purge before loading modules in a submit file
ml purge
ml ABINIT/8.10.3 Armadillo/9.700.2 CDO/1.9.5 GOTM/5.3-221-gac7ec88d NCO/4.8.1 NCO/4.9.2 OpenFOAM/6 OpenFOAM/7 OpenFOAM/v1912 Rosetta/3.7 Siesta/4.1-MaX-1.0 Siesta/4.1-b4 Singular/4.1.2 XCrySDen/1.5.60 XCrySDen/1.6.2 deal.II/9.1.1-gcc deal.II/9.1.1-intel
